description: Twelve square frames on a near-black charcoal ground. Each holds ONE centred mass, floating, occupying maybe 55-75% of the frame with a wide even dark margin on all four sides. Nothing touches the frame deliberately; a couple spill off the bottom (1985692, 1446330) and that reads as accident rather than intent. The construction is flat, semi-transparent polygons -- discs, hexagons, squares, triangles, diamonds -- stacked and slightly rotated so the alpha overlaps produce banded greys and sawtooth stepped edges. Perhaps 6-15 shapes per token. No line work, no texture, no small marks beyond a handful of tiny orange dots and squares (1203347 has one dot low-left of the core; 1366079 and 1985692 have a small orange square; 1475115 has two or three dots). Palette is tightly held: warm neutral greys, a bone/parchment off-white, and exactly one saturated colour, an ochre-amber orange. The orange is ALWAYS the innermost element and the greys always the outer shell, in all twelve, without exception. So the thing it is a picture OF, if anything, is a shell around a warm core -- an egg, a sealed capsule, a seed in a husk, a coin or badge with a boss in the middle, a mask. 1243682 and 1446330 push furthest toward figure: bilateral lobes at the top corners and a tapering bottom read as ears/shoulders, a beetle or a heraldic shield or a small hooded animal. Most tokens are bilaterally symmetric about the vertical axis (1203347, 1243682, 1283437, 1446330, 1985692); 1561509, 1835793 and 1991107 are rotated/irregular and read looser. What the twelve share: the centred single mass, the shell-and-core armature, the flat translucent polygon language, the same three-value palette. How they differ is essentially two independent choices from a small vocabulary -- outer silhouette (circle: 1203347, 1475115, 1283437; hexagon: 1310661, 1366079, 1733538; square/rect: 1561509, 1985692, 1835793; diamond: 1991107; lobed creature: 1243682, 1446330) crossed with core shape (circle: 1203347, 1733538, 1561509; diamond: 1283437, 1991107, 1243682; square: 1366079, 1985692, 1835793; blob: 1475115). 1835793 is the one true outlier and not in a good way: it is the only frame with a filled mid-grey background PANEL behind the object instead of the near-black void, which reads as a different render rather than a variant. Across the three market states the change is loud and unmistakable. Neutral is cool and pale: grey shell, muted ochre core, often a bone-white backing disc. Stress warms and darkens the entire object into brown-amber, the bone-white backing DISAPPEARS (1283437 and 1243682 lose their outer circle entirely, changing the silhouette from round to shield/cluster), the core swells and saturates to a hot ochre (1283437 stress: the diamond nearly doubles), and NEW content appears -- a row of orange circular beads along the upper edge in 1203347 stress and 1310661 stress that is simply not present in neutral. Recovery returns to the cool register but overshoots into something paler and calmer than neutral: the bone disc comes back larger and brighter, greys soften, the core shrinks and goes chalky (1283437 recovery is a big pale circle with a modest diamond; 1203347 recovery is the whitest frame of its three). So the row order reads neutral/stress/recovery as cool, hot, cooler-still. At 120px what survives is: the centred silhouette, the shell/core relationship, the single orange accent, and the state temperature. What does NOT survive is internal structure -- 1446330 and 1475115 collapse into undifferentiated grey mush at 120, and the stepped polygon edges that give 1985692 and 1561509 their character turn into staircase noise. At browse size the twelve resolve to roughly six or seven distinguishable things, because several are the same two decisions repeated: 1203347, 1733538 and 1561509 all read as grey-blob-with-orange-circle, and 1366079 and 1985692 both read as grey-mass-with-orange-square. Compositionally all twelve make the identical decision -- centred, floating, symmetric margin -- so there is strong focal hierarchy within a frame (orange core beats grey shell beats black void) and zero compositional variation between frames.
